question: The Bengal Famine took a huge toll of life and was called as tragedy in unpreparedness. In which year did it occur?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1943**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bengal Famine of 1943**, was a** catastrophic event in the Bengal province** of British India **during World War II**.
 
• An estimated** 2.1–3 million**, out of a population of 60.3 million people,** died of starvation, malaria, or other diseases exacerbated by malnutrition, population displacement, unsanitary conditions, and lack of healthcare.**
 
• While natural disasters like cyclones and crop diseases contributed to the initial food scarcity, the **Wartime policies of the British colonial administration worsened its impact**.
 
• This included the **'denial policy', **which involved the removal or destruction of boats, bullock carts, or any other means of transport to prevent them from falling into Japanese hands if they invaded India, effectively disrupting distribution networks.
 
• It resulted in enormous loss of life and demonstrated the imperial government's lack of provision for its subjects in times of extreme peril. 
 
• It **led to major shifts in policy and a reconsideration of agricultural and famine relief strategies**, both in the immediate aftermath and after India's independence in 1947.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Madras Famine of 1876 - 1878** was a catastrophic event.
 
• It affected the **Madras Presidency in British India**, now a large part of southern India.
 
• It was part of the larger Indian Famine of 1876–78 that spread across various Indian regions, resulting from severe drought, cyclones and ineffective government policies.
 
• It led to dire food shortages and widespread deaths due to starvation.
 
• The Famine Commission of 1880, sparked by the tragedy, ultimately led to systemic changes, shaping India's future famine prevention strategies.
 
• Thus, the Madras famine was not only a humanitarian disaster but also a poignant moment in India's colonial history, influencing future policy reform.
